feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}+4?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/d67114a9865ca54cdf14798e779cfa9c00e71598ba652d6fccdcf686f86e20ef.png)

 

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/d6dcae76f7fe89188ef449c817f7e7af48c25763077d1daee9626d2f26b1a78a.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $4$ units up to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}+4.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,3)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/529dfc1ef1bc6f0ff58addca6cf27c5039a6cf18c5a307c06a153a3d56040ede.png)
